answers.nothing: The new renderRouteTree, the shared restoreAfterEach helper, the persona/account test and the raised floors (182 for the two added tests) all do what the commit message and the DD-08 text say.

restoreAfterEach pops its restores last-in-first-out, so nested configureApiClient/configureScreenLoader calls restore correctly; an empty pending list is a no-op and an empty routes or options object falls back to defaults.
Restores run in afterEach even when a test fails, and the only throw on this path (buildRoutes([]) with no navigation destination) is asserted by the existing test.

The only state that outlives a call is the module-level pending array in restoreAfterEach.ts. It is drained after each test, and each test file gets its own module instance, so writers do not interleave.

Each removed per-file restores array and afterEach (client.test, router.test, screenStatus.test, and adapterRestores in render.tsx) is replaced one-for-one by restoreAfterEach, and the removed router and provider wiring in router.test now lives in renderRouteTree.

The change builds no keys, ids or paths that tell things apart; the only name-like construction is the shell.persona.<id> translation key, which comes from the closed PERSONA_IDS list.

`configureApiClient` and `configureScreenLoader` each return a restore function, and `restoreAfterEach` takes exactly that `() => void`. `createMemoryRouter`, `buildRoutes(features)` and `createAppStore` are called as their declarations allow.
The `RenderOptions` and `RootState` shapes are unchanged. `renderRouteTree` returns the same shape as before, and `router.test` reads `.router` from it correctly.

`restoreAfterEach` registers one `afterEach` that pops every pending restore in last-in-first-out order, so each install is undone after every test, including failing ones. The api-client adapters installed by `render.tsx`, `client.test.ts` and `router.test.tsx`, and the screen loaders installed by `router.test` and `screenStatus.test`, all go through it.
